stories.title: El Nino’s wrath: Brace yourself for impact
stories.summary: The forecast is increasingly ominous, with a strong, possibly record-breaking El Nino about to play havoc with the world’s weather and oceans. Droughts, wildfires, floods and severe heatwaves are set to affect millions of people across Asia and the globe. While El Ninos are part of the earth’s natural cycle, climate change is making these events more dangerous. What is El Nino? El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, triggering worldwide changes in winds, atmospheric pressure and rainfall patterns and pushing up global temperatures. These events happen every two to seven years. Strong events are less frequent. Burning coal, oil and gas releases greenhouse gases that are heating up the planet. A rapidly warming planet in combination with a powerful El Nino is like pouring fuel on a fire. La Nina events are the opposite. Westward-blowing trade winds intensify, causing more warm water to pool around the maritime continent. This results in more rain and cooler weather in this region.
